config.title: Build typed analytics event catalog

intro.title: Build typed analytics event catalog
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed analytics event catalog to safely track user interactions in an application. You will learn to use TypeScript's core feature—type safety—to define a set of possible events, ensuring that only valid event names and data are logged. This involves creating custom types, interfaces, and a function to record events, which helps prevent runtime errors. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe system for managing analytics events in your projects.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building robust analytics systems in applications like e-commerce dashboards, where tracking user interactions (e.g., button clicks, form submissions, page views) must be type-safe and consistent. Developers use typed event catalogs to ensure events like 'add_to_cart' or 'checkout_start' are properly defined with required properties, preventing runtime errors in tools like Google Analytics or Mixpanel. In practice, this enables teams to maintain a single source of truth for analytics events across features such as user onboarding flows, A/B testing panels, or admin modals, improving data reliability and developer collaboration.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the structure of an analytics event.
Implement a typed array to catalog multiple analytics events with consistent properties.
Apply union types to categorize events into distinct, predefined groups.
Manipulate event data by adding and updating entries in the typed catalog.
Initialize and render a function that processes and logs events from the catalog.
Integrate type guards to validate event categories at runtime.
Configure a reusable utility function to generate standardized event payloads.

steps.title: Import TypeScript and define the AnalyticsEvent type
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript type definition named 'AnalyticsEvent' with required properties: 'eventName' (string), 'timestamp' (number), and 'userId' (string).
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to define a new type with the specified properties and their TypeScript types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A type definition that can be used to enforce structure for analytics event objects throughout the application.
successCriteria: The 'AnalyticsEvent' type is defined with 'eventName: string', 'timestamp: number', and 'userId: string' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the type definition is incomplete. Make sure all three properties (eventName, timestamp, userId) are included with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The type definition doesn't match what's needed. Remember to create a type named 'AnalyticsEvent' with eventName (string), timestamp (number), and userId (string) properties.

steps.instruction: Below your AnalyticsEvent type, define a new type named EventCatalog that uses TypeScript's Record utility to organize analytics events by category.
steps.hint: Use Record<string, AnalyticsEvent[]> to create a type where each key is a category name and the value is an array of AnalyticsEvent objects.

steps.title: Create sample analytics event data
steps.instruction: Create a typed constant named 'sampleCatalog' that matches the EventCatalog type. Initialize it with at least one sample event for each category (e.g., 'pageView', 'buttonClick', 'formSubmit').
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword with type annotation ': EventCatalog' and assign an object with your sample events.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a typed constant 'sampleCatalog' that contains sample analytics events organized by category.
successCriteria: A constant named 'sampleCatalog' is declared with type 'EventCatalog' and contains at least one sample event per category.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'sampleCatalog' is typed as 'EventCatalog' and contains sample events for each category.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've declared a constant named 'sampleCatalog' with the correct type annotation and sample data structure.

steps.title: Create the AnalyticsCatalog component with typed props
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named AnalyticsCatalog that accepts a prop of type EventCatalog. The component should return a simple div wrapper for now.
steps.hint: Define a TypeScript interface for the component's props, then create the component that receives those props.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional React component named AnalyticsCatalog is created with typed props that accept an EventCatalog.
successCriteria: The AnalyticsCatalog component is defined with a props interface that includes an EventCatalog property, and the component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component accepts a prop of type EventCatalog and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Remember to create a functional component named AnalyticsCatalog that accepts EventCatalog as a prop.

steps.title: Add basic component structure and return statement
steps.instruction: Inside the AnalyticsCatalog component, add a return statement that returns a <div> element containing an <h1> with the text 'Analytics Event Catalog'.
steps.hint: The return statement should be the last line inside your component function, and it should return JSX wrapped in parentheses.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now return a basic structure with a heading when rendered.
successCriteria: The AnalyticsCatalog component has a return statement that returns a <div> containing an <h1> with the exact text 'Analytics Event Catalog'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement includes both the <div> wrapper and the <h1> with the exact text 'Analytics Event Catalog'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete yet. Remember to add a return statement that returns JSX with a <div> containing an <h1> with the text 'Analytics Event Catalog'.

steps.title: Map through event categories and display category headers
steps.instruction: Inside your AnalyticsCatalog component, use Object.entries to iterate through the catalog prop and render a heading for each event category.
steps.hint: Object.entries(catalog) gives you an array of [categoryName, events] pairs. Map over this array to create a heading element for each category.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render a heading for each event category in the catalog, using the category name as the heading text.
successCriteria: Object.entries is used to iterate through the catalog prop, and a heading element is rendered for each category with a unique key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using Object.entries(catalog) to get the categories and rendering a heading for each one.

steps.hint: After displaying the category header, use events.map() to create list items or divs for each event. Access event.name and event.properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each category section now displays a list of its events with their names and properties.
successCriteria: The component maps through the events array within each category and renders event details.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping through the events array and displaying both the event name and properties.
